names.significance: The sahasrāra at the crown of the head, where She is the yoginī Yākinī (528–534); compare 105, sahasrārāmbujārūḍhā.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: सर्वे वर्णाः सर्ववर्णाः; सर्ववर्णैः उपशोभिता सर्ववर्णोपशोभिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarve varṇāḥ sarvavarṇāḥ; sarvavarṇaiḥ upaśobhitā sarvavarṇopaśobhitā
samasa.explanation: (1) sarva-varṇa 'all colors' (karmadhāraya). (2) The participle upaśobhitā 'adorned, made beautiful' is the head and takes the colors in the instrumental.

names.meaning: She who is resplendent with all colors
names.significance: Yākinī shines with every color. Since varṇa also means 'letter', it is traditionally read too as 'adorned with all the letters', which are said to cover the petals of the thousand-petaled lotus.

meaning_check.note: 'many colors' → 'all colors' (sarva).

names.previous_split_issues: varṇopaśobhitā was one row; it is varṇa + upaśobhitā, joined by guṇa.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: सर्वाणि आयुधानि सर्वायुधानि; सर्वायुधानि धरति इति सर्वायुधधरा
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarvāṇi āyudhāni sarvāyudhāni; sarvāyudhāni dharati iti sarvāyudhadharā
samasa.explanation: (1) sarva-āyudha 'all weapons' (karmadhāraya). (2) dharā 'holding' (√dhṛ + the agent suffix a) takes them as its object.

names.meaning: She who holds all weapons
names.significance: Yākinī bears the weapons of all the other yoginīs: every power is hers.

meaning_check.note: 'known' is not in the name.

names.previous_split_issues: sarvāyudha was one row; it is sarva + āyudha 'weapon'.

sandhi.rule: the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ)

samasa.vigraha: शुक्ले संस्थिता शुक्लसंस्थिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: śukle saṃsthitā śuklasaṃsthitā
samasa.explanation: The participle saṃsthitā 'abiding' is the head and takes śukla 'semen, vital essence' in the locative.

names.meaning: She who resides in the semen, the vital essence
names.significance: Śukla is the seventh and last of the bodily tissues (dhātu), the essence of all the others; it belongs to Yākinī.

meaning_check.note: 'the vital essence' added to make clear that śukla here is the dhātu, not the color white (as in 522).

sandhi.rule: visarga sandhi: final s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66), which after a and before a voiced consonant becomes u (6.1.114 haśi ca); a + u then gives o (6.1.87)

samasa.vigraha: सर्वतः मुखानि यस्याः सा सर्वतोमुखी
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarvataḥ mukhāni yasyāḥ sā sarvatomukhī
samasa.explanation: The adverb sarvatas 'on all sides' qualifies mukha 'face'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose faces are on all sides'. mukha takes the feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54).

components.note: mukha with the feminine -ī of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who has faces turned in all directions
names.significance: Yākinī faces every direction; so the Bhagavad Gītā describes the Supreme as having eyes, heads and faces everywhere (sarvato'kṣiśiromukham).
names.previous_split_issues: sarvato was glossed 'all'; it is sarvatas 'on all sides' in its sandhi form.

sandhi.rule: vṛddhi: a + o → au (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: सर्वे ओदनाः सर्वौदनाः; सर्वौदनैः प्रीतम् सर्वौदनप्रीतम्; सर्वौदनप्रीतम् चित्तम् यस्याः सा सर्वौदनप्रीतचित्ता
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarve odanāḥ sarvaudanāḥ; sarvaudanaiḥ prītam sarvaudanaprītam; sarvaudanaprītam cittam yasyāḥ sā sarvaudanaprītacittā
samasa.explanation: (1) sarva-odana 'all kinds of rice' (karmadhāraya). (2) …odana-prīta 'pleased by them' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) It qualifies citta 'mind', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose mind is pleased by all kinds of rice'.

components.note: citta, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose mind is pleased by all kinds of rice offerings
names.significance: Yākinī accepts every offering, as all the yoginīs are gathered in her.

meaning_check.note: Reworded to follow the compound: odana is rice, and citta 'mind' is the head of the bahuvrīhi.

names.previous_split_issues: sarvaudana was one row (sarva + odana, joined by vṛddhi); cittā was glossed 'consciousness' — here it is the mind.

sandhi.rule: yaṇ: ī before an unlike vowel becomes y (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

samasa.type: karmadhāraya, with the possessive suffix -in (svarūpa itself a karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: याकिनी च असौ अम्बा च याकिन्यम्बा; स्वम् रूपम् स्वरूपम्; याकिन्यम्बा स्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति याकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: yākinī ca asau ambā ca yākinyambā; svam rūpam svarūpam; yākinyambā svarūpam asyāḥ asti iti yākinyambāsvarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) yākinī-ambā 'Mother Yākinī' (karmadhāraya of apposition). (2) sva-rūpa 'own form, true nature' (karmadhāraya). (3) The possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115) is added to the whole: 'She whose own form is Mother Yākinī'.

components.meaning: Yākinī, the yoginī of the sahasrāra

components.note: sva 'own' + rūpa 'form' + the possessive suffix -in, feminine -ī; n becomes ṇ after r (Pāṇini 8.4.2)

names.meaning: She who has the form of Mother Yākinī
names.significance: This name closes the Yākinī group (528–534). With her the section of the seven yoginīs (475–534) ends.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS tidied; ambā 'mother' translated.

names.previous_split_issues: yākinyambā was one row; it is yākinī + ambā 'mother', joined by yaṇ (ī → y).

components.meaning: svāhā, the call with which an oblation is offered to the gods

names.meaning: She who is Svāhā, the call with which offerings are made to the gods in the fire
names.significance: Svāhā is personified as the consort of Agni, through whom the gods receive the oblations; She is the power that makes the offering reach them.

meaning_check.note: Shortened: the old wording described the ritual rather than the name.

components.meaning: svadhā, the call with which offerings are made to the ancestors

names.meaning: She who is Svadhā, the call with which offerings are made to the ancestors
names.significance: Svadhā is the counterpart of svāhā: with it offerings are made to the pitṛs, the ancestors; personified, she too is a form of the Goddess.

meaning_check.note: Made specific: svadhā is the call of offerings to the ancestors.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101), between this name and 536; the avagraha ऽ marks the merged a. Bhāskararāya reads svadhā + amatiḥ here, not svadhā + matiḥ (matiḥ is already name 445).

samasa.vigraha: न मतिः अमतिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: na matiḥ amatiḥ
samasa.explanation: The negative na, reduced to a before a consonant (Pāṇini 6.3.73 nalopo nañaḥ), compounds with mati 'understanding': 'non-understanding', ignorance.

names.meaning: She who is in the form of ignorance or nescience
names.significance: Ignorance too is Her power: the Devīmāhātmya calls Her both the supreme knowledge that is the cause of liberation and the cause of bondage in saṃsāra. The next name, medhā, gives the other side.

components.meaning: intelligence, wisdom; the power of retaining knowledge

names.meaning: She who is in the form of wisdom (medhā)
names.significance: Medhā is the intelligence that grasps and retains knowledge, especially of the sacred texts; with 537 She is both ignorance and wisdom.

names.meaning: She who is in the form of the Vedas
names.significance: Śruti, 'what was heard' by the seers, is the Veda; She is its very substance.

meaning_check.note: 'vedas' capitalized.

names.meaning: She who is smṛti, the remembered tradition that rests on the Vedas
names.significance: Smṛti, the dharma texts and Purāṇas that draw out the meaning of the Veda, follows śruti (539); smṛti is also memory, and the Devīmāhātmya praises the Goddess who abides in all beings as memory (smṛtirūpeṇa).

meaning_check.note: ITRANS tidied ('smRiti', 'vedas').

samasa.vigraha: न विद्यते उत्तमः यस्याः सा अनुत्तमा
samasa.vigraha_iast: na vidyate uttamaḥ yasyāḥ sā anuttamā
samasa.explanation: The negative na with uttama 'higher, best' makes a bahuvrīhi: 'She than whom there is none higher'. Before a vowel na becomes an- (Pāṇini 6.3.73–74, a morphological change, not sandhi).

components.note: the negative na before a vowel
ud + the superlative suffix -tama; uttama with the feminine -ā

names.meaning: She who is the best; She who is not excelled by anyone
names.significance: None surpasses Her; She is the highest.

verse_notes.note: Names 491–494 complete Rākiṇī of the anāhata: her twelve attendant śaktis, her food and her name.
Lākinī of the maṇipūra (495–503). Name 498 is a phrase, not a compound: ḍāmaryādibhiḥ 'by Ḍāmarī and the rest' keeps its instrumental ending and is joined to āvṛtā by sandhi (-bhir āvṛtā).

external_sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the avagraha ऽ marks the a that has merged

verse_notes.note: Kākinī of the svādhiṣṭhāna (504–513). The avagraha marks the a of ati: name 508 is atigarvitā.
Name 509: medo- is medas 'fat' in its sandhi form (s → o before the voiced n).

external_sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the avagraha ऽ marks the a that has merged

verse_notes.note: Sākinī of the mūlādhāra (514–520). The avagraha marks the a of asthi 'bone': name 516 is asthisaṃsthitā.
Name 520 closes Sākinī; Hākinī of the ājñā begins at 521 (521–527).
Name 526 is haridrānna + ekarasikā ('delighting solely in turmeric-rice'); compare 90, kulāmṛtaikarasikā.
Yākinī of the sahasrāra (528–534), who gathers the attributes of all the others: all colors, all weapons, faces in every direction.

external_sandhi.rule: ā + a → ā (savarṇa-dīrgha, Pāṇini 6.1.101), marked by the avagraha; then the visarga of amatiḥ becomes r before the voiced m (final s → ru, 8.2.66, kept as r after i)
visarga after i becomes r before a voiced sound or a vowel (final s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66; ru is kept as r, since the change to u applies only after a)

verse_notes.note: The yoginī section ends with 534. Name 537 is amatiḥ 'ignorance' (svadhā + amatiḥ; the avagraha shows the a), not matiḥ, which is name 445; 537 and 538 (medhā) pair ignorance and wisdom. 535–536 are the sacrificial calls svāhā and svadhā.

report.summary: Checked all 51 names of ślokas 101–110 against text.json — the yoginī section from Rākiṇī's attendants to Yākinī (491–534), then svāhā … anuttamā — with sandhi at every member junction (including visible prefix junctions such as ni + sthā → niṣṭhā, sam + yutā, anu + itā), layered samāsa analyses with pausa-form vigrahas, and the meanings against that analysis. Most meanings were tidied (ITRANS, words not in the name, compounds whose head was missed, such as 501, 505, 512, 519); none needed replacing. Name 498 is shown to be a two-word phrase (ḍāmaryādibhir āvṛtā), and 537 amatiḥ is explained as Bhāskararāya's reading of svadhā'matiḥ. No problem was found in the Sanskrit text.
